samples.marker: ScreenConnect 25.2.4: stock vendor client; deployment unknown
evidence: Exact SHA-256 match to filF23135311FD413DA3A6A8DD4B38FBBC4 extracted independently with 7z from ScreenConnect_25.2.4.9229_Release.msi.

Downloaded MSI SHA-256 0dabef8ee019bc34bf315794df0f5321ee8122e18d87411ab5f79f6ef73f46a0. Its Authenticode content digests and timestamp verify; certificate revocation prevents current trust acceptance.

Specimen Authenticode digest and signer cryptography verify. Signer SHA-256 82b4e7924d5bed84fb16ddf8391936eb301479cec707dc14e23bc22b8cdeae28. DigiCert CRL signature independently verified with the embedded issuer certificate; serial 0B9360051BCCF66642998998D5BA97CE is revoked with Key Compromise reason. Retain the existing suspicious certificate trait.
Disassembled 3397 managed methods using dnfile/dncil. CLR entry token 0x060003eb is ScreenConnect.Program.Main. No manifest resources or embedded relay configuration.

Main selects RunFile/RunFileElevated, StartService, Rerun and RunRole modes; otherwise parses supplied URL/query or ClickOnce ActivationUri. Without launch parameters it throws an explicit error. Host/port/session/key/access token are supplied through ClientLaunchParameters.

Vendor ScreenConnect.Core dependency parses URL/query parameters and calls EnforceConstraint. ScreenConnect.Client dependency manages transport and message routing. These were obtained from the independently downloaded installer.

Clipboard synchronization and file sending traverse permission/connection attributes and virtual streams into EnqueueOutgoingMessage. Screen capture, input control, audio, printing and service-start/UAC code implement the stated remote-administration role; no unrelated hostile routine found.

RunFile/RunFileElevated launch caller-selected files. StartService uses the adjacent ClientService executable and normal runas elevation when needed, or explicitly supplied credentials; this is not a UAC bypass.
samples.why_collected: Named AV verdicts overwhelmingly identify RemoteAdmin, ScreenConnect PUA or hacktool capabilities. Malware collection and high sandbox score remain concerning, but the bytes match the vendor distribution; the record supplies no operator, relay, installer configuration or execution history proving abuse.
missing_context: Adjacent configuration and libraries actually deployed
samples.source_limitations: Triage overview API returned HTTP 401; supplied sandbox score was not treated as observed execution.

samples.identification: PixelPilot Copilot VS Code extension 3.0.9, a Kilo/OpenCode coding-agent derivative
samples.marker: PixelPilot 3.0.9: coding agent; fixed grammar/runtime false hits
evidence: Read VSIX manifest/package, deminified extension.js and inspected UI bundles, source maps, activation, settings, authentication, remote-session and execution handlers. Ordinary bundling/minification rather than a hidden decoder.

Parsed the 52-byte Bun module graph records from the .bun PE section. Recovered all 748 modules, including entry id 13 B:/~BUN/root/src/index.js. The 151 MB executable is Bun 1.3.14 hosting readable Kilo CLI code, WASM grammars and native UI/PTY/watcher dependencies.

Bundled native modules are watcher-vc9az7tm.node, rust_pty-fazdxkv2.dll and opentui-2q8rnfnn.dll. Inspected PE structure and PTY exports with rz-bin; these implement watcher/UI/pseudoterminal operations used by the agent.

Activation registers VS Code panels and commands. ServerManager generates a random 32-byte server password, then launches the bundled CLI with [serve,--port,0]. UI connects to the local HTTP/SSE service using Basic authentication. Server middleware validates KILO_SERVER_PASSWORD.

CLI entry builds its command parser, initializes application storage/SQLite and telemetry, and dispatches the requested command. Bash and file tools pass through permission-request handlers before shell/file operations. Auto-approval and remote sessions are user-configurable capabilities.

API token is explicitly entered or received through the documented vscode URI callback. It is supplied to the configured PixelPilot backend and provider clients. API/user/me fetch and API/track event POST match account/usage telemetry behavior; no unrelated credential sweep-to-send chain found.

CLI authenticates supported model providers, manages its own auth.json, loads configured MCP/plugins, downloads supported assets and implements cloud-session import/export. These are exposed agent functions, not evidence of a concealed implant.

PixelPilot homepage returned HTTP 200 and unauthenticated /api/user/me returned HTTP 401. api.kilo.ai returned HTTP 200. The claimed GitHub repository API returned HTTP 404, leaving independent source comparison unavailable.

Bun runtime and browser grammar/tokenizer bundles account for many network/crypto/process strings. In particular, Rust ClosePseudoConsolekernel32.dll caused an Elex substring match; tasklist and application names appeared in highlighting catalogs; getClass was a local ts-morph test helper; FileOutputStream was a decoded tokenizer vocabulary word.
A composite correlated KaTeX settings.isTrusted with an unrelated xterm ARIA live region and falsely inferred agent-control disclosure. Removed that composite rather than suppressing the bundle.
samples.why_collected: No external detection names or malicious execution context were supplied for this sample. A large unsigned executable inside a startup-activated extension, broad command/file/network capabilities, minified code and the demonstrated grammar/runtime false positives plausibly explain heuristic collection. This remains an inference; the original collection reason is unavailable.
missing_context: Publisher provenance or independently accessible source for this exact build
User agent sessions and configured MCP/plugins
samples.analysis_limits: Static analysis only. Cleave reports source-flow budgets and string retention limits on large bundles; recovered module code and manual path tracing supplemented those gaps. No specimen or bundled executable was run.

samples.marker: Node.js types 25.9.3: exact npm declarations; no runtime code
evidence: Read the entire file and inspected cleave facts, including comments, references and decoded-string views. It contains license comments and TypeScript triple-slash lib/path directives, with no executable statements.

Fetched @types/node 25.9.3 from npm; node/index.d.ts is byte-for-byte identical, including SHA-256. Referenced .d.ts dependencies are supplied in that declaration archive and specify Node/TypeScript type definitions, not runtime loaders.

The github.com/nodejs/node documentation URL is a license/provenance reference in a comment, not a network operation. Relative paths to crypto, child_process and network declarations request type information and do not invoke those facilities.
samples.why_collected: The original malware label is not explained by these bytes. A legitimate declaration file can be collected as a dependency of a hostile package or inherit a bundle-level label; that possibility cannot identify the parent or establish its verdict.
missing_context: Original containing package or collection context

coverage_changes: All moved observations retain their matchers and effective type/platform scopes. Unsupported inherited attacker mappings were removed. The GCP credential filename was also raised from baseline to notable.
The tasklist/application-name composite now states neutral co-occurrence within 512 bytes rather than claiming process discovery from two unrelated references up to 200 lines apart.

The tasklist token matcher rejects immediate pipe-prefixed catalog alternatives. JVM metatype requires a direct receiver chain. FileOutputStream requires a parsed symbol. Elex typo requires a whole NUL-terminated name.
Removed extension-announces-agent-control: no relationship between ARIA status and trusted-input checks was established.

Audited ancestor directory consumers: neutral paths, runtime/error strings, generic method/configuration names and HTTP headers no longer contribute via attacker-objective directory selectors. Exact consumers were updated explicitly; no broad target-directory substitutions were introduced.
